anchors.1: Major defects; fails most essential requirements.
anchors.2: Partial success; material omissions or errors remain.
anchors.3: Meets core requirements with limited, disclosed defects.
anchors.4: Strong result; minor defects only; evidence is complete.
anchors.5: Excellent, complete, repeatable result with independently checkable evidence.

dimensions.definition: Factual and technical correctness against a task-specific reference.
Claims are supported by accessible, attributable evidence and provenance.
Coverage of explicit requirements and edge cases.
Repeatability across runs; graceful handling of failures and uncertainty.
Policy compliance, permission boundaries, privacy and safe failure behaviour.
Confidence and uncertainty match the available evidence.
Latency, tool calls, token/resource use and cost relative to task.
Another reviewer can reproduce the procedure and inspect artifacts.
